title: Chapter 10.  Environment - Yamuna, the Ridge & Air Pollution

blocks.content: Delhi's environment chapter is dominated by two of India's most persistently newsworthy ecological crises - Yamuna river pollution and winter air pollution/smog - making this one of the highest current-affairs-yield chapters in the entire book.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Yamuna river ecosystem health is a critical urban environmental focus in Delhi.
Air pollution peaks during winter due to smog formation, stubble burning, and meteorological factors.
The Ridge represents a key biodiversity hotspot and natural barrier against desertification in the region.
Environmental management requires integrated action across river rejuvenation, air quality control, and green space conservation.

blocks.content: The Yamuna flows through Delhi for a relatively short stretch (about 22 km) but this stretch is disproportionately significant because it receives the bulk of the city's untreated/partially-treated sewage and industrial effluent, making the Delhi stretch one of the most polluted sections of the entire river.

The river's Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) levels within Delhi frequently far exceed safe bathing-water standards, and visible pollution phenomena - notably toxic white foam on the river surface, especially during Chhath Puja celebrations when devotees wade into the water - have become a recurring, heavily photographed news story each year.

Major drains (nullahs) carrying sewage into the Yamuna within Delhi include the Najafgarh Drain (the single largest contributor of pollution load) among dozens of others; cleanup efforts have included the Yamuna Action Plan (a long-running, only partially successful Centre-state river-cleaning initiative) and more recent Delhi-government-specific interventions.
Environment - Yamuna, the Ridge & Air Pollution

★ EXAM POINT: The toxic foam on the Yamuna during Chhath Puja is one of the most visually iconic and frequently referenced current-affairs images associated with Delhi's environment - remember it is caused by high phosphate content from detergents/industrial effluent combined with low water flow.

Delhi consistently ranks among the world's most polluted major cities during winter months, driven by a combination of vehicular and industrial emissions, construction dust, and - critically - seasonal crop-residue (stubble) burning in the neighbouring states of Punjab and Haryana, whose smoke drifts into the Delhi-NCR airshed during October-November under specific wind and temperature-inversion conditions.

The Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) is the principal regulatory mechanism used to manage air-quality emergencies, imposing escalating restrictions (from Stage I 'Poor' to Stage IV 'Severe+') on construction activity, vehicle usage (including odd-even vehicle rationing schemes trialled in past years), and industrial operations as Air Quality Index (AQI) readings worsen.

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) - a statutory body created by a 2021 Act of Parliament - coordinates air-quality policy across Delhi and the neighbouring NCR states, given that pollution sources and airflow patterns cross state boundaries and cannot be tackled by Delhi's government alone.

cells: Dust-control measures, stricter monitoring of construction sites
Enhanced parking fees, intensified public transport frequency
Ban on non-essential construction/demolition; restrictions on BS-III petrol/BS-IV diesel vehicles
Entry ban on trucks (except essential goods); potential closure of schools; work-from-home advisories

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: GRAP and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM, 2021 Act) are the two most-tested institutional/regulatory names in this chapter - CAQM is notable as one of the few statutory bodies with jurisdiction spanning Delhi AND parts of neighbouring states specifically for pollution management.

items: Questions frequently test the geographical significance of the Delhi Ridge as an extension of the Aravalli Range.
Focus on key air quality indicators, PM2.5/PM10 dynamics, and thermal inversion causing winter smog.
Understand major pollution parameters (such as Biological Oxygen Demand) affecting the Yamuna River stretch in Delhi.

The Delhi Ridge (Chapter 1) remains the city's principal forested tract; biodiversity parks along the Yamuna floodplain (such as the Yamuna Biodiversity Park) represent more recent ecological-restoration initiatives distinct from the Ridge.

Delhi hosts several city forests and protected green spaces, including the Central Ridge Reserve Forest, Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary (in south Delhi, bordering Haryana's Aravalli tract), and numerous smaller municipal parks and biodiversity parks developed in recent decades.
Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary is Delhi's principal formally notified wildlife sanctuary, protecting Aravalli scrub-forest habitat and associated fauna at the NCT's southern edge.
Yamuna flows through Delhi for ~22 km, receiving heavy pollution load, notably from the Najafgarh Drain; toxic Chhath Puja foam is an iconic recurring image.
GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan) manages air-quality emergencies in 4 escalating stages tied to AQI bands.
Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) - statutory body (2021 Act) coordinating cross-state pollution policy.
Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary - Delhi's principal wildlife sanctuary, protecting Aravalli scrub-forest at the NCT's southern edge.
